Discussion states both patients were premedicated and thought to potentially have aseptic meningitis; these sentences explicitly say "both"/"These patients" but give no drug names for the antihistamine, no doses and no times for case 1.

patients.label: Case 2: 7-year-old girl with anti-TIF-1γ-positive juvenile dermatomyositis who developed intracranial hypertension and papilledema after monthly IVIG

identity_evidence.quote: A 7-year-old girl with progressive proximal muscle weakness and rash was diagnosed with JDM

attribution_limitations: The elevated ICP was first attributed to prolonged steroid use, and later the authors report growing suspicion that IVIG might be responsible; both are hedged or time-limited attributions.
The IVIG dose is printed as "95 mg (2 g/kg)", mixing mg with g/kg.

Text says muscle enzyme levels returned to normal and, earlier, persistent elevations of muscle enzymes and inflammatory markers, while Table 1 columns (diagnosis, increased ICP, 1 year after IVIG discontinuation) have no flags and no column matching either text time.
Glaucoma is named once with no laterality, grade or later follow-up; "increased intraocular pressure (IOP)" is also stated without values.
Transition to mycophenolate mofetil is stated as part of the decision to taper IVIG; whether it was administered is not separately stated.
Discussion states increased ICP was identified "after six to eight doses of IVIG" in both patients; case 2 text states 11 total doses and the ICP finding six months after starting IVIG.
The source says increased intraocular pressure (IOP) "worsened to" bilateral grade 3 papilledema; IOP and papilledema are different findings, so the wording may mean intracranial pressure.

The discussion says neither patient had any predisposing risk factors, without naming the factors (the preceding sentence lists headache history and high-dose IVIG as aseptic meningitis risks, and the same sentence says both received high-dose IVIG).

The IVIG dose is printed as "95 mg (2 g/kg)", mixing mg with g/kg.

Text says muscle enzyme levels returned to normal and, earlier, persistent elevations of muscle enzymes and inflammatory markers, while Table 1 columns (diagnosis, increased ICP, 1 year after IVIG discontinuation) have no flags and no column matching either text time.
Glaucoma is named once with no laterality, grade or later follow-up; "increased intraocular pressure (IOP)" is also stated without values.
Transition to mycophenolate mofetil is stated as part of the decision to taper IVIG; whether it was administered is not separately stated.
Discussion states increased ICP was identified "after six to eight doses of IVIG" in both patients; case 2 text states 11 total doses and the ICP finding six months after starting IVIG.
The source says increased intraocular pressure (IOP) "worsened to" bilateral grade 3 papilledema; IOP and papilledema are different findings, so the wording may mean intracranial pressure.

The discussion says neither patient had any predisposing risk factors, without naming the factors (the preceding sentence lists headache history and high-dose IVIG as aseptic meningitis risks, and the same sentence says both received high-dose IVIG).
